script.title: How Air India Saves Crores Flying Over Iraq #shorts

segments.text: Flying through Iraq is saving Air India crores in jet fuel.
segments.broll: airplane flying above clouds golden hour wide
broll_alt: commercial jetliner flying high altitude wide

segments.text: Direct flights to New York and Newark are taking this shorter route.
segments.broll: flight navigation display cockpit close up
broll_alt: glowing digital world map route lines
airplane cockpit instruments night shot close up

segments.text: Jet fuel makes up nearly forty percent of an airline's operating expenses.
segments.broll: airport tarmac fuel truck aerial shot
broll_alt: jet engine turbine rotating slow motion

segments.text: By cutting flight time, Air India expects a ten percent drop in fuel burn.
segments.broll: pilot hands operating cockpit controls close up
broll_alt: pilot side profile looking out window
airplane wing flap adjusting mid flight

segments.text: That means saving lakhs of rupees on every single flight, yaar.
segments.broll: busy airport terminal passengers walking wide

segments.text: Will ticket prices get cheaper, or will airlines keep the extra profit?
segments.broll: passenger looking out airplane window medium shot
broll_alt: person booking flight on smartphone close up
airplane landing on runway sunset wide

script.description: Air India is using Iraq airspace for direct flights to New York and Newark, aiming for 10% fuel savings. Here is how airline route economics impact flight costs and profitability. #AirIndia #AviationIndia #PaisaDecoded

facts_to_verify.claim: Air India starts using Iraq airspace for New York and Newark direct flights, likely expecting 10% fuel savings.
Jet fuel (Aviation Turbine Fuel) typically accounts for around 30-40% of an airline's total operating costs in India.
